# The capillary-wave verification harness and the open free surface

*TensorSPH, verification record. Generated by `benchmarks/capillary_wave/make_doc.py` from `benchmarks/capillary_wave/open_surface_audit.json` -- do not edit by hand.*

## 1. Case and problem

`benchmarks/verification_ledger/waivers.json` used to carry the entry

> `benchmarks/capillary_wave/`: harness only (capillary-wave dispersion check), no committed artifact - evidence debt E1

so the repository shipped a capillary-wave harness with **no committed evidence** that the capability works. `benchmarks/capillary_wave/validation.py` is the end-to-end comparison against Lamb (1932); it commits no output either, and running it at HEAD on its own `resolution` case aborts inside two capillary periods. This page replaces that silence with a measurement.

The physical case is a **standing capillary wave on an open free surface**: a 2-D pool held by a free-slip (`clamp`) bottom and sides, no gravity, no physical viscosity, perturbed as `eta = A cos(kx)` with the mode matched to the domain width so that the side boundaries are crest and trough.

| parameter | value |
|---|---|
| wavelength `lambda` | 20.0 mm |
| wavenumber `k = 2 pi/lambda` | 314.2 1/m |
| water depth `H` | 20.0 mm |
| `kH` (deep-water factor `tanh kH`) | 6.28 (0.99999) |
| initial amplitude `A` | 0.50 mm (= 0.5 dx) |
| particle spacing `dx` | 1.00 mm (20 points per wavelength) |
| surface tension `sigma` | 7.2 N/m |
| density `rho0` | 1000 kg/m^3 |
| sound speed `c0` | 10 m/s |
| analytic `omega` (Lamb 1932 Art. 267, `g = 0`) | 472.5 rad/s |
| analytic period | 13.30 ms |
| physical restoring acceleration `omega^2 A` | 111.6 m/s^2 |
| physical particle velocity `u_ref = A omega` | 0.236 m/s |

The audit horizon is 2.0 capillary periods (the harness itself simulates four to five).

## 2. What was done

`benchmarks/capillary_wave/open_surface_audit.py` performs three measurements on that case and records a status row instead of an exception:

1. **Harness as-is.** `validation.run_case` is called with the harness's own `resolution` parameters. Whatever it does -- abort or finish -- is recorded.
2. **Initial-state decomposition.** The acceleration of the untouched initial state is measured by `rhs` with surface tension on and off, so the CSF contribution is isolated from the density/pressure transient; the discrete curvature field of the same interface (`csf_fields`) is compared with the perturbation's own curvature `k^2 A`.
3. **Variant sweep and amplitude ladder.** 10 solver configurations (density renormalisation, mass calibration, both free-surface pressure-closure donor semantics, the legacy CSF scheme, a square lattice, a higher sound speed) and two amplitudes (`A/dx = 0.5, 2`) are marched over the same horizon. Admissibility follows Adami, Ihmsen & Adams (2012): a surface-tension run may only be graded when the spurious current is below 10 % of the capillary velocity scale, here `u_ref = A omega`.

Everything is deterministic and CPU-only; the whole audit is 278 s of wall clock on the repo checkout.

## 3. Results

### 3.1 The harness does not run at HEAD

| item | value |
|---|---|
| case | `resolution` |
| status | **aborted** |
| abort step | 336 |
| exception | `1 particle(s) left the box at step 336; the case is not a free-surface standing wave any more` |

### 3.2 The first step is already unphysical

| configuration | `max|a|` [m/s^2] | `p99 |a|` | median `|a|` on the surface shell | `rho_min/rho0` | `p_max` [Pa] | `max|a| / omega^2 A` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `csf_off` | 302.9 | 302.9 | 64.8 | 0.491 | 599 | 3x |
| `csf_on_mass_calibrated` | 3070.2 | 2989.8 | 481.9 | 0.491 | 599 | 28x |
| `csf_on` | 3070.2 | 2989.8 | 481.9 | 0.491 | 599 | 28x |
| `csf_on_density_renormalization` | 1821.7 | 1739.4 | 626.8 | 0.866 | 0 | 16x |

The CSF contribution to the very first step is 2767 m/s^2 (**25x** the wave's own restoring acceleration of 111.6 m/s^2). The acceleration with surface tension off is not zero either: the uncalibrated lattice kernel-sum bias builds 599 Pa of spurious pressure, which the Tait clamp releases at the free surface; mass calibration removes it, but the CSF term is then still the dominant acceleration in the problem.

### 3.3 Where the CSF force comes from: curvature noise on a flat surface

For the perturbation, the analytic interface curvature is `k^2 A = 49.3 1/m`. The discrete curvature of the *same* interface, measured on the particles that carry the surface delta function, is:

| lattice | `h/dx` | curvature operator | interface particles | `kappa_rms` [1/m] | `|kappa|` p95 | `|kappa|` max | noise / signal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hex | 1.3 | `mls` | 63 | 192.9 | 305.6 | 339.0 | 3.9x |
| hex | 1.3 | `fit_quadratic` | 63 | 294.8 | 736.0 | 886.4 | 6.0x |
| hex | 1.5 | `mls` | 63 | 186.1 | 274.9 | 286.6 | 3.8x |
| hex | 1.5 | `fit_quadratic` | 63 | 233.9 | 611.5 | 620.5 | 4.7x |
| square | 1.3 | `mls` | 60 | 202.6 | 323.0 | 323.6 | 4.1x |
| square | 1.3 | `fit_quadratic` | 60 | 278.0 | 619.0 | 619.0 | 5.6x |
| square | 1.5 | `mls` | 60 | 193.3 | 285.9 | 285.9 | 3.9x |
| square | 1.5 | `fit_quadratic` | 60 | 247.1 | 560.3 | 560.3 | 5.0x |

The curvature noise is 3.8x to 6.0x the physical signal on every lattice and both operators; the force per unit volume scales with `sigma kappa delta_s`, which is what section 3.2 measures directly.

### 3.4 No knob rescues it

| variant | status | `max|v| / u_ref` | `rho_min/rho0` | omega error [%] | fit residual | admissible (Adami) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `baseline` | aborted @ step 336 | 29.4 | 0.233 | - | - | **no** |
| `density_renormalization` | completed | 17.7 | 0.866 | -61.5 | 0.23 | **no** |
| `mass_calibrated` | aborted @ step 336 | 29.4 | 0.233 | - | - | **no** |
| `pressure_closure_all_donors` | aborted @ step 222 | 27.1 | 0.233 | - | - | **no** |
| `pressure_closure_interior_2` | aborted @ step 62 | 27.2 | 0.233 | - | - | **no** |
| `legacy_csf` | aborted @ step 464 | 31.1 | 0.233 | - | - | **no** |
| `square_lattice` | aborted @ step 311 | 27.2 | 0.504 | - | - | **no** |
| `sound_speed_20` | aborted @ step 1364 | 55.4 | 0.233 | - | - | **no** |
| `renorm_plus_calibrated` | completed | 17.7 | 0.866 | -61.5 | 0.23 | **no** |
| `renorm_plus_legacy` | completed | 15.1 | 0.866 | -50.2 | 0.25 | **no** |

7 of 10 variants abort before the horizon; 0 run is admissible under the Adami limit. Note that `rho_min/rho0` and the abort step move in opposite directions for the closure variants: they raise the shell density but inject more momentum at the surface, which is the same trade-off measured on the Young-Laplace ladder.

### 3.5 A larger amplitude does not help either

| variant | status | imposed `A` [mm] | measured `a(0)` | omega error [%] | fit residual | `max|v| / u_ref` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A=0.5dx/renorm` | completed | 0.50 | -0.63 mm | -61.5 | 0.51 | 17.7 |
| `A=0.5dx/baseline` | aborted @ step 336 | 0.00 | - mm | - | - | 29.4 |
| `A=2.0dx/renorm` | completed | 2.00 | +0.78 mm | -61.5 | 0.63 | 4.2 |
| `A=2.0dx/baseline` | aborted @ step 376 | 0.00 | - mm | - | - | 6.8 |

A larger amplitude raises the physical signal, but the fit residual stays high and the extracted frequency does not follow the analytic one: the measured mode is dominated by the surface transient, not by the wave.

## 5. Notes and limitations

1. **Scope.** The audit covers the standing-wave geometry the harness uses. It says nothing about closed interfaces: the Young-Laplace work on a drop reaches -34 % with a 0.03 spurious current and the two-phase control is inside 5 %, so the failure here is specific to a *one-sided, open* support.
2. **Not a defect of the measuring chain.** The abort is a guard: when a particle leaves the box the case is no longer a free-surface standing wave. The guard was kept, not weakened, and the audit records the abort instead of grading the run.
3. **The amplitude estimator is not the blocker.** `column_elevation` quantises the surface into horizontal bins of one particle spacing; at `A = 0.5 dx` that is comparable to the signal, which is why section 3.5 repeats the case at `A = 2 dx`. Even there the fit residual stays high, so the limitation is in the force, not in the estimator.
4. **What would change the verdict.** A curvature operator or colour field that is smooth at the particle scale on a one-sided support (the `curvature_color_smoothing` option of `csf_fields`, interface smoothing, or a delta-function renormalisation) has to bring the section 3.3 noise ratio below one *before* the wave can be graded; the tests below pin the current numbers so the fix cannot pass unnoticed.

## 6. Error verdict

| key quantity | reference | measured | error | below 3 % ? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| capillary frequency `omega` | Lamb (1932) 472.5 rad/s | no admissible reading | not measured (spurious current 15.1x to 55.4x `u_ref`, Adami limit 0.1) | **no -- WITHHELD** |
| viscous damping `gamma = 2 nu k^2` | Lamb (1932) | no admissible reading | not measured | **no -- WITHHELD** |
| curvature of the flat interface | 0 1/m | +148.2 1/m (signed mean, `hex`, `h/dx=1.3`) | `kappa_rms` 192.9 1/m vs signal 49.3 1/m | **no** |

**Explicit answer to the platform question.** The capillary-wave dispersion and damping claims are **not** within 3 % of Lamb (1932) -- they are not measurable at all at HEAD, because the run that would produce them is inadmissible (spurious current above the Adami limit in every variant, and an abort in the harness itself). The capability stays graded WITHHELD, now with a committed root cause and a committed noise floor instead of an unregistered directory.

## 7. Reproduction

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python benchmarks/capillary_wave/open_surface_audit.py  # ~3 min
PYTHONPATH=src python benchmarks/capillary_wave/make_doc.py
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_capillary_wave_open_surface.py -q
```
